verdict.tagline: Fast-paced cooperative action backed by an incredible soundtrack.

you cannot tolerate vague item descriptions

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players note the lack of an in-game tutorial and vague item descriptions, alongside great cooperative multiplayer and standout music.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that item descriptions are vague and the game lacks an in-game tutorial explaining core mechanics and item effects.

citations.review_text:
as a new player, playing the game blindly was pretty frustrating because the game takes the roguelite aspect way too literally by actively refusing to explain anything to you, your first few runs are entirely out of your control whether they are won or lost because you are just picking up random ??? items so you can "learn" them instead of making choices that matter for your current run. 

only later on once you have a good collection of items learned you are allowed to think about what works good on which characters, good synergies, etc. even still, after killing the final boss the game just gives you a completely random timer and says "good luck" while you figure out what is even happening, its not really intuitive having to pause the game to search "what do i do after i kill the boss ror2" or to just sit on the boss platform for 3 minutes

once you get past humoring the game design that is the very mediocre new player experience, the game is really enjoyable and feels super rewarding. actually knowing which items do what, or experimenting with stacking items is much more fun than blindly guessing. unlocking new survivors is really fun too when you learn the item pool, since you already have a pretty good idea of what items should and shouldn't work on them. besides the potentially frustrating start, it's overall a very enjoyable game.

Risk of Rain 2 feels like a game where the developers rely on modders to finish their work. There's barely a tutorial, item descriptions are ridiculously vague, and one of the most popular mods literally just adds information that should've been in the game from the start.

Even Simulacrum, the mode I actually enjoyed, has glaring issues. Waves don't properly wait for players to choose items, you can't save between waves without mods, and enemies sometimes spawn in unreachable areas.

claims.claim: Unlockable items, characters, and abilities are locked behind achievements that require specific and difficult challenges.

citations.review_text:
I personally don't understand the hype and praise for this game.

I've got all but the latest DLC, and with almost 80 hours at this time, I don't think I've truly had fun with it. I think there's three primary reasons why, even though I might be alone on this.

[b]1. It's slow paced[/b]
Maps can be quite large and open, and at the start of runs, the movement speed is just too low. Also the need for money in the beginning means you have to wait for enemies to spawn which drags out too.

[b]2. The run strategy is confusing[/b]
Is it best to speedrun to prevent enemies from scaling too much, should I try to get every item in hopes of outscaling them, or is there a middle ground, and where is that? I was wondering this both in the beginning and all the way to ~60h when I decided to look it up.

[b]3. The challenges are tedious and luck based[/b]
All unlockables like items, characters, and abilities are locked behind achievements. Many of them are ok and actually spice up the aproach to gameplay a little, but so many of them are so specific and hard to pull off either due to complexity or luck that they feel more like chores than challenges. Some examples are: "heal 1000 hp at once" (only possible with one specific rare item or with tons of max-hp items), "complete a challenge run without taking damage" (has to be done with a melee character, requiring you to get close), or the challenges that force you to play on the highest difficulty.

There were of course some other issues I had, like no option for sprint-by-default, and item descriptions being vague, but those were fixed with mods or in a later update.

TL;DR: The game has a lot of content, but it's just too tedious, confusing and unfun to go through and unlock it all.

As someone who's a roguelike fanatic, Risk Of Rain 2 is a must-play for all the other roguelike lovers out there. As with any roguelike it can be quite challenging at first figuring how to survive through the first 5 maps and fight your way to the Lunar Commencement Zone, yet once you've figured it out and pushed past the curve, you will absolutely obliterate the game (or yourself in that matter lol)


Can be a massive time-sink and a grindy game trying to unlock the achievements for heroes and items, and that will be most likely your biggest frustration with this game, but as is with any other good roguelike. Hours are easily invested into this game without you ever realising. The biggest strengths of ROR2 lies in its simple yet addicting gameplay loop sitting on top of some of the most phenomenal video game OST you've ever graced your ears with.


Genuinely of the best games of all time, and that is not said lightly. i'm currently enjoying every moment of playing this game with my friend Delcy, though a solo experience can be quite fun as well.


10/10 Will risk it all in the rain.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that disconnecting during a multiplayer run causes a complete loss of progress with no way to continue the run alone.

citations.review_text: Risk of Rain 2 is one of my favorite games to just turn my brain off and play with friends. The soundtrack, art style, and overall atmosphere are fantastic, and the round-based progression makes it ridiculously easy to get sucked into another run. The problem is that the game can be pretty demanding depending on how far a run goes, especially with a lot of effects happening at once. Hosting is also a problem since multiplayer relies on player-hosted sessions instead of dedicated servers. If the host crashes, the entire run can be ruined, and because runs can take so long, there's no real way for someone to drop out and come back without losing their progress. It's a great game, but the multiplayer infrastructure really holds it back sometimes.

i got disconnected at the end of a run and lost 57min just because. I can't even continue the run alone. 

Don't get me wrong the game is absolutely amazing and the music is fire but the fact that it doesn't have that simple feature just sucks, will download a mod i guess

citations.review_text: New dlc added a different final boss scaling which is forcibly enabled in eclipse(hard mode) which makes it borderline unplayable for base game players without the dlc scaling and it has been more than a month since this obviously idiotic change without any fix in sight, which would be incredibly easy to fix. If you think it sounds fun for every dlc they add to break the game and you like having to wait for gearbox to fix it again go ahead and buy it you'll for sure have fun with the hopoo games content until they decide it goes against their intended experience and remove it next year

The new devs keep updating the game with very little care to what was there before. Every update has made the game slightly worse in tiny ways and the devs have given no indication that they will change this. They also do not provide an easy way to downpatch the game, so any bad changes they make are permanent.
DLCs come out regularly but take forever to be patched, leaving sometime game-breaking bugs in the game for months.

DO NOT play this game if you arent ready to install mods to smooth out the rough edges. 

also this is BARELY a multiplayer game. It is heavily advertised as one but the netcode is so atrocious that if you arent hosting a multiplayer game you are having a SIGNIFICANTLY worse time.

If you are on console, you cant get mods so dont even bother with the game honestly.

TLDR: only buy this game if you are ready to download mods, never play multiplayer, and suffer through most mods breaking when an update or DLC rolls around and everyone is forced onto the new patch.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the music and soundtrack as a major highlight of the experience.

citations.review_text:
Music 10/10 
Vibes 11/10
Fun with friends infinite/10

A video put it best describing this game, "I don't want to die because I don't want to stop hearing the music."

“Just one more run.” – me, 203.5 hours ago

Risk of Rain 2 is the kind of roguelike that eats your whole night without you noticing. You land on a strange planet with nothing, and 40 minutes later you’re a blur of fire, lightning, and missiles, deleting bosses before their health bars finish loading.

I’ve been playing since the first game, and seeing my favorites make the jump to 3D was a treat. Huntress is still my go-to: she blinks around the map, fires arrows that lock onto whatever is closest, and makes kiting a whole horde feel effortless. Engineer is my other main for the opposite reason. You set up turrets, drop your bubble shield, and watch your little army copy every item you’ve stacked and shred everything in sight.

How I play: Monsoon only, with the Artifact of Sacrifice and the Artifact of Swarms. Sacrifice removes the chests, so enemies drop your items, and Swarms doubles every spawn. You can’t hide in a corner and farm. You have to throw yourself into the horde to get stronger, and twice as many enemies means twice as many chances at loot. It turns every run into a nonstop feeding frenzy, and once you play this way it’s hard to go back.

The soundtrack: Chris Christodoulou’s score is worth the price of the game on its own. Some of my favorite moments with this game weren’t even playing it. They were sitting my friends down and making them listen to the soundtrack. It’s heavy, atmospheric, and strange, and it fits the feeling of being stranded on an alien planet perfectly. If the music doesn’t sell you, nothing will.

The good:

Stacking items is pure chaos in the best way. Every run builds into something ridiculous, and finding a combo that breaks the game is half the fun.
The difficulty climbs with the clock, so you’re always racing to get strong before the game outscales you.
Every survivor plays differently, so there’s always a reason to try someone new, even if you keep going back to your favorites.
Co-op is a blast. Nothing beats a squad screami…
best roguelike ever, characters are unique, very engaging gameplay, amazing areas with some of the best music i've ever heard

I really did not like this game at first, but after forcing myself to get over the grueling learning period, I found myself captured by this games world, characters, and of course THE MUSIC. Despite all the problems this game has, it remains as an amazing work of art that's always a joy to experience.

I honestly play this game purely for the music, no joke.
The music in this game is fabulous, i don't enjoy the gameplay as much and the last paid dlc has a lot of problems but the music and design is awesome.

While I haven't been the greatest fan of the past few updates, I still have this on the top as my favorite game of all time. Great replayability, amazing soundtrack, unique characters that each play the game entirely differently, not to mention the hundreds of item synergies that exist with the concept of stackable items. I will always recommend this game to gamers who are looking for a fresh take on the roguelike genre.
